clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952 and the purchase of the apple orchard, within the following months: June became homesick and wrote daily to her sister Edna, then withdrew from Walter as he worked long hours in the trees; Glen had fights at his new school; Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money; June kept to her bed for weeks that winter and clashed with Walter over money for new trees; by September 1953 she joined the church choir and her anxiety eased. These shifts in the household and between the couple and their son show a family unsettled by the move.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan: Walter drank heavily most nights and clashed with Glen over blame for the loss; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed; by October 1969 Walter stopped drinking and took work pruning other men's trees, where his functioning rose. The shifts moved from Walter's symptom and the conflict with Glen through the household's reorganisation and the children's reactions.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen's loss of his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975: Glen sat in the truck in the yard for hours, out of work most of that year; he and Marian fought loud fights at night over money and he took a second job cleaning offices; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight, then kept to her room with distance from her mother; Walter began drinking again after six years off it; by March 1976 Glen started driving a delivery truck for the feed store, and by June Nora's functioning rose as she ate again and made the track team. The shifts in the household centre on the loss of Glen's work and its ripple through the couple and the children.

clusters.name: Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma's move into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990 after selling her farm: Nora clashed with Wilma over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows, then took his mother's side; Wilma took over Lily's care; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Nora's eczema flared on both hands and she clashed with Sam most nights, then drove over twice a week to take her mother's side; by June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and by August Nora's eczema cleared. The shifts show the household pulled into conflict over Wilma's arrival and authority, settling when she moved out.
